analysis:
Reviewed scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (head lines 566-1064). The change is test-only: it replaces VALID_SIZES with PRODUCTION_SIZES = {8x16, 12x32} and remaps PLAN_LANES to those sizes, and the patch excerpt is truncated. The visible tests assert several security-relevant router properties:
- Invalid lane config and size grammar fail before any plane request (lines 590-612).
- Job sizes are sent only when DARKBLOOM_JOB_SHAPES is exactly 'on' (614-664).
- A sized lane accepts only the exact labels of its size, and malformed grants fall back (666-690).
- Hostile plane text cannot inject workflow commands or markdown (734-746).
- darkbloom-route.yml has no permissions, secrets, checkout or id-token (758-789).
- Routed jobs are read-only with bounded timeouts (831-847).
- Release and credentialed workflows keep literal Blacksmith runners and never reference self-hosted or darkbloom labels (959-978).
- The watchdog and hourly workflows are least-privilege (980-1046).
These tests do not weaken any control. No production code is changed in the supplied units, and none of the threat-model assets (provider keys, attestation, prefix cache T-041, TB-011 authorization) are touched. The retained T-041 definition is unrelated to this CI-routing test. Remaining uncertainty: the workflow files (provider-plan.yml and others) that these tests validate are not in the supplied units. The interim-size claim, that the plane does not sign 4x16 and 4x24, rests on a comment I could not verify. The truncated patch could hide other changed lines in the earlier part of the file, but the changed ranges listed are small and in constants only.
